constraints: Dimension count must stay consistent with jobs[].delivery, jobs[].pickup, and shipments[].amount.
businessRules: Hard constraint: for every dimension d, running onboard load <= capacity[d] at every step of the route.
Pickups increase load mid-route, so a load that is feasible at the depot can still breach capacity between a pickup and its delivery.
When violated, the offending task is placed in result.unassigned[] with a capacity reason; the solve still returns HTTP 200 and result.code == 0.

Multi-dimension: capacity [10,100] with all deliveries/pickups/amounts 2-D and within both bounds -> accepted.
Negative-validation: negative capacity value like [-5] -> 400.
Negative-validation: dimension mismatch (capacity [10,100] but a job delivery [5]) -> 400.
Negative-infeasible: a single job whose delivery exceeds every vehicle's capacity -> in result.unassigned (capacity reason), still HTTP 200, result.code 0.

Negative-infeasible: N jobs each delivery [1] on capacity [N] all fit; the (N+1)th on the same route breaches -> unassigned.
Interaction: zero-quantity demand is always capacity-feasible (a weightless stop).

allRules.summary: Route balancing / penalty terms are best-effort and never override hard constraints (C1–C7); infeasible tasks stay unassigned regardless of balancing configuration.
allRules.rule: Balancing and penalty terms under options.objective (e.g. minimize_visits_over_threshold) and options.constraint (vehicle_overtime_penalty, visit_lateness_penalty, max_vehicle_overtime as a soft constraint) are best-effort and subordinate to all hard constraints (C1–C7: capacity, time windows, precedence, max-stops, max-duration, skills, zones, depots). A task infeasible under hard constraints stays unassigned in result.unassigned regardless of balancing weights. Enabling balancing must never cause an otherwise-feasible task to become unassigned; it only shifts the order of feasible assignments.
testingGuidance: Positive: all jobs feasible under hard constraints + balancing options enabled -> all jobs still assigned (assert assignment count only, never the specific route distribution).
Negative-infeasible: a job infeasible under a hard constraint (e.g. impossible time window) stays unassigned regardless of balancing weights (assert unassigned reason).

allRules.summary: A stop is feasible only if the vehicle can start it within a window (or within lateness tolerance) and still fit the shift; early arrival waits.
allRules.rule: Arrival must fall inside one of a task's time_windows, or within max_visit_lateness after it; early arrival waits (inflating elapsed/working time). The whole route including service and waiting must finish within the vehicle's time_window. An impossible window (ends before the earliest reachable arrival, beyond tolerance) sends the task to result.unassigned (time-window reason); HTTP stays 200. This applies uniformly to job steps, shipment pickup/delivery steps, depot anchor points, and break windows — each must satisfy its own window + lateness constraint.

Shipment: delivery window [09:00,09:30], max_visit_lateness 15, nearest vehicle arrives 09:40 -> accepted within lateness.
Break: break time_windows [12:00,13:00], vehicle arrives 12:30 -> break scheduled at 12:30.
